words.meaning: to give a false impression of something or fail to show its true nature
words.example: Her calm tone belied how worried she was about the deadline.

words.meaning: to establish an idea, habit, or system so firmly that it is difficult to change
words.example: Adding more exceptions would entrench a process that already frustrates customers.

words.meaning: to overcome a difficult obstacle or problem
words.example: The team surmounted several technical setbacks and launched on schedule.

words.meaning: to publicly criticize something as wrong or harmful
words.example: Local business owners decried the sudden increase in permit fees.

words.meaning: to separate complicated parts or make a confusing situation easier to understand
words.example: We need to disentangle the billing issue from the separate shipping delay.

phrases.example: A three-hour sales pitch on Saturday morning? Hard pass.

phrases.meaning: unavailable or unable to respond for a period of time
phrases.example: I will be out of pocket during my flight, but I can reply this evening.

phrases.meaning: to develop problems or turn out badly
phrases.example: The rollout went sideways when the payment system stopped working.

phrases.meaning: to try doing or solving something
phrases.example: I have never repaired this kind of faucet, but I will take a crack at it.

phrases.meaning: to be deeply involved in complicated details or overwhelmed by them
phrases.example: We are getting in the weeds, so let us return to the main decision.
